title: Configurationally Locked Ridaifen-B Analogs as Potent Ebola Virus Entry Inhibitors.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Ebola virus disease poses a global public health threat due to emerging outbreaks, high mortality rates, and limited treatment options, underscoring the need for effective therapies. The unique and critical role that EBOV glycoprotein (GP) plays in the viral life cycle makes it an attractive target for antiviral drug discovery.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study reports on the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a series of cyclized ridaifen-B-based inhibitors with enhanced antiviral activity and selectivity against EBOV.
analysis.methods: The antiviral activity and selectivity of the compounds were evaluated against EBOV and Marburg virus. Site-directed mutagenesis was used to indicate inhibitor binding at the EBOV GP1/GP2 fusion loop. The compounds displayed favorable in vitro pharmacokinetic parameters, which encouraged testing the in vivo rapid PK for hit compound 41.
analysis.main_results: Several compounds exhibited nanomolar potency inhibiting EBOV-GP-mediated entry and submicromolar potency against Marburg virus entry.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the potential of 1,2-dihydronaphthalene and tetrahydronaphthalene derivatives as valuable leads for the development of potent antifiloviral agents targeting EBOV among other filoviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The identification of potent inhibitors targeting the EBOV GP fusion loop provides a promising avenue for the development of new therapeutics to combat filovirus infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific details regarding the study design, sample size, or statistical analysis, limiting the assessment of the evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the critical need for effective therapies against Ebola virus disease, a global public health threat characterized by high mortality and limited treatment options. The researchers focused on the EBOV glycoprotein (GP), a key component of the viral life cycle, as a target for antiviral drug discovery. They designed, synthesized, and evaluated a series of cyclized ridaifen-B-based inhibitors. The results demonstrated that several compounds exhibited nanomolar potency in inhibiting EBOV-GP-mediated entry and submicromolar potency against Marburg virus entry. Site-directed mutagenesis indicated that the inhibitors bind to the EBOV GP1/GP2 fusion loop. The compounds also showed favorable in vitro pharmacokinetic parameters, leading to further testing of a hit compound in vivo. The study concludes that 1,2-dihydronaphthalene and tetrahydronaphthalene derivatives are valuable leads for developing potent antifiloviral agents.

title: Quantifying the heterogeneity and determinants of Ebola Zaire transmission during the 10th outbreak in DRC, 2018-2020.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health problem of sustained Ebola Zaire transmission in the DRC during 2018–2020, where armed conflict and community mistrust complicated control. It aimed to quantify transmission heterogeneity and identify its determinants in this large outbreak.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective observational study reconstructed transmission chains for 3481 confirmed and probable Ebola cases from August 1, 2018, to June 25, 2020, using Ministry of Health and MSF surveillance data. Transmission events linked 2402 individuals into 415 chains.
analysis.methods: Transmission chains were reconstructed and the offspring distribution was modelled with a Bayesian negative binomial framework, correcting for incomplete contact tracing to estimate the effective reproduction number (Reff), dispersion parameter (k), and the proportion of cases responsible for 80% of transmission. Individual-level determinants were assessed with a regression extension adjusting for covariates.
analysis.main_results: Overall Reff was 1.00 (95% CI 0.92–1.08) with k 0.29 (0.26–0.32); 17.8% of cases generated 80% of transmission. Non-isolation (IRR 1.79), death outside a treatment centre (IRR 4.34), and unfollowed contact status (IRR up to 4.48) predicted more secondary cases; vaccination cut transmission by about 60%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted transmission as heterogeneous and stable over time, with superspreading driven by operational gaps in contact tracing, isolation, and vaccination delivery rather than new contexts. They reported that Reff alone is an insufficient summary of epidemic potential and highlighted modifiable determinants as key targets for control.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings imply that strengthening contact tracing, isolation, and vaccination delivery—especially during insecurity—can disproportionately reduce transmission. They also suggest surveillance should monitor dispersion (k) alongside Reff to anticipate epidemic potential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relied on routine surveillance data with incomplete contact tracing, which may bias estimates of transmission chains and determinants. Despite this, the Bayesian correction and consistent dispersion over fluctuating Reff strengthen the evidence base, warranting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational study quantified Ebola Zaire transmission heterogeneity during the 2018–2020 DRC outbreak using surveillance data from 3481 cases. It reconstructed 415 transmission chains and estimated an overall effective reproduction number of 1.00 with a dispersion parameter k of 0.29, indicating that 17.8% of cases generated 80% of onward transmission. Transmission remained overdispersed even when Reff fluctuated, underscoring that superspreading is a stable structural feature. Regression analyses identified modifiable determinants—non-isolation, death outside treatment centres, and poor contact tracing—each associated with substantially more secondary cases, while vaccination reduced onward transmission by approximately 60%. The authors conclude that operational gaps in contact tracing, isolation, and vaccination delivery, rather than knowledge gaps, shaped transmission, particularly during periods of insecurity. These findings highlight the need to monitor dispersion alongside Reff for epidemic potential and to prioritize strengthening these interventions to curb future outbreaks.

title: Antibody Therapy Targeting GP in Treatment of Ebola Virus Infection

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the development and application of antibody therapies targeting the glycoprotein (GP) of the Ebola virus (EBOV) for the treatment of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD). The central question revolves around the efficacy and potential of these antibodies in combating EBOV infections, particularly those caused by the Zaire ebolavirus (ZEBOV) species. The review also explores the broader implications of these therapies for public health and global economies, especially in regions like West Africa that have been severely impacted by EBOV outbreaks.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review covers Ebola virus disease outbreaks from 1976 to 2025, predominantly focusing on the Zaire ebolavirus (ZEBOV) species. The review includes the development and approval of antibody-based therapeutics such as ZMapp, Inmazeb, and Ebanga, which have been authorized for the emergency treatment of ZEBOV infections. The review also discusses the identification of numerous antibodies with broader antiviral spectra that are currently under development.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that a deeper understanding of the characteristics of neutralizing antibodies targeting the EBOV glycoprotein (GP) will accelerate the development of novel antibody therapies. This understanding will also provide guidance for the rational design of next-generation drugs against EBOV infection. The review highlights the importance of these therapies in combating EBOV infections and their potential impact on public health and global economies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not explicitly report on controversies or evidence gaps in the current understanding of antibody therapies for EBOV. However, it implies that further research is needed to fully understand the characteristics of these antibodies and their potential applications in treating EBOV infections.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research is needed to develop a deeper understanding of the characteristics of neutralizing antibodies targeting the EBOV glycoprotein (GP). This understanding will be crucial for the development of novel antibody therapies and the rational design of next-generation drugs against EBOV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This review article by Sandra Chiu, Jiazhao Gao, and Rui Gong, published in Health and Metabolism in 2026, focuses on the development and application of antibody therapies targeting the glycoprotein (GP) of the Ebola virus (EBOV) for the treatment of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD). The review covers Ebola virus disease outbreaks from 1976 to 2025, predominantly focusing on the Zaire ebolavirus (ZEBOV) species. It includes the development and approval of antibody-based therapeutics such as ZMapp, Inmazeb, and Ebanga, which have been authorized for the emergency treatment of ZEBOV infections. The review also discusses the identification of numerous antibodies with broader antiviral spectra that are currently under development. The review concludes that a deeper understanding of the characteristics of neutralizing antibodies targeting the EBOV glycoprotein (GP) will accelerate the development of novel antibody therapies. This understanding will also provide guidance for the rational design of next-generation drugs against EBOV infection. The review highlights the importance of these therapies in combating EBOV infections and their potential impact on public health and global economies.

title: Editorial: Integrated genomic and systems approaches to unravel host-virus interactions in viral infectious diseases

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to decode host-virus interactions in viral infectious diseases through integrated multi-omics and systems approaches, aiming to advance the development of novel diagnostics and host-targeted therapeutics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The editorial reviews seven primary research articles investigating host-virus interactions across various viral diseases, including VZV, ZIKV, Ebola, DENV, SARS-CoV-2, coronaviruses, and ASFV, using diverse models such as CSF, brain organoids, patient blood, and porcine macrophages.
analysis.methods: The included studies employed cross-system analysis, LASSO regression, functional siRNA knockdown, LC-MS and GC-MS metabolomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and mathematical modeling to identify biomarkers and validate antiviral mechanisms.
analysis.main_results: CSF proteomics in VZV CNS infection revealed elevated protein abundance in IFN-1 signaling and BBB disruption pathways, while ZIKV multi-system transcriptomics identified 22 shared ISGs and 11 diagnostic biomarker candidates, and Ebola virus disease modeling showed delayed IFN-I responses in non-survivors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as demonstrating the power of integrated multi-omics to uncover context-dependent IFN-I signaling, temporal immune dynamics, and conserved host vulnerabilities, thereby advancing mechanistic investigation and therapeutic target identification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the utility of multi-omics integration for biomarker discovery and the importance of appropriate cell and patient models, offering a foundation for improved in vitro models, antiviral strategies, and prognostic stratification.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the editorial synthesizes findings from seven primary studies with varying designs and models, and the provided evidence does not explicitly assess generalizability or bias.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial synthesizes seven primary research articles that utilize integrated multi-omics and systems approaches to decode host-virus interactions across diverse viral infectious diseases. The studies investigate viruses targeting the central nervous system (VZV), Zika virus (ZIKV), Ebola virus disease (EVD), dengue virus (DENV), SARS-CoV-2, coronaviruses, and African swine fever virus (ASFV). Key findings include the identification of CSF proteomic signatures in VZV CNS infection, the discovery of interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) regulation and diagnostic biomarkers in ZIKV, and the elucidation of delayed IFN-I responses in Ebola non-survivors. The authors conclude that cross-cutting themes such as the centrality and context-dependence of IFN-I signaling, the importance of temporal immune dynamics, and the utility of multi-omics integration for biomarker discovery are critical for advancing the development of novel diagnostics and host-targeted therapeutics.

title: It’s not just virology: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda demands a wider public health response

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for a broader public health response to the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the DRC and Uganda, highlighting that epidemics stem from biological pathogens as well as social inequities, environmental disruption, fragile health systems, and persistent armed conflict.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary on the current Ebola outbreak in the DRC and Uganda, focusing on the Bundibugyo virus.
analysis.methods: The authors analyze the outbreak by examining the conditions that allow the virus to spread, such as fear-provoking symptoms and high mortality, and the social determinants that contribute to its persistence.
analysis.main_results: The authors observe that while Ebola captures headlines due to its fear-provoking symptoms and high mortality, the underlying conditions that facilitate its spread receive far less attention.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets the outbreak as a multifaceted crisis requiring a wider public health response that goes beyond virology to address social and systemic factors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that effective control of Ebola requires addressing social inequities, environmental disruption, and fragile health systems alongside medical interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a commentary and lacks empirical data, limiting its ability to provide quantitative evidence; the evidence strength is low due to its descriptive nature.

analysis.summary_en: This commentary highlights the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the DRC and Uganda as a multifaceted crisis requiring a broader public health response that addresses social inequities, environmental disruption, and fragile health systems, not just virological factors. The authors argue that while Ebola's fear-provoking symptoms and high mortality capture headlines, the underlying conditions enabling its spread are often overlooked. The study emphasizes the need for a holistic approach that integrates social and systemic interventions with medical measures to effectively control the outbreak.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the persistent public-health threat posed by Ebola virus disease and the need to translate lessons from the 2014–2016 West African epidemic into preparedness for future mass gatherings such as the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors present a reflective essay that synthesizes international guidance and recent experience in preparing for mass events, focusing on the role of epidemiological surveillance, diagnostic capacity, institutional coordination, and societal education.
analysis.methods: The work is based on document analysis of international organizational reports and experiential evidence from mass-event preparedness, integrating qualitative synthesis rather than primary data collection or laboratory assays.
analysis.main_results: The essay concludes that prevention must be framed as an ongoing educational process that transforms knowledge into responsible behavior, with childhood education identified as a key strategy for building a culture of prevention.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the Ebola epidemic’s legacy as demonstrating that scientific advances alone are insufficient without societal preparedness, emphasizing the novelty of positioning education and preventive culture as central pillars of resilience.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings imply that integrating risk communication and preventive education into public-health planning can enhance societal resilience to future health emergencies, particularly in the context of large-scale events.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base is limited to a qualitative synthesis of documents and experiences, lacking primary data, quantitative outcomes, or causal inference, which constrains the strength of the conclusions to low.

analysis.summary_en: This reflective essay examines how lessons from the 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic can inform preparedness for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, arguing that epidemiological surveillance and institutional coordination must be paired with societal education and a preventive culture. The authors synthesize international guidance and recent mass-event preparedness experiences to conclude that prevention is an ongoing educational process requiring childhood education to build resilient societies. They emphasize that the greatest legacy of Ebola is not merely scientific advances but the transformation of knowledge into responsible behavior. The work highlights the need to integrate risk communication and preventive education into public-health planning for future health emergencies.

title: Screening and monitoring of travellers returning from countries affected by Bundibugyo virus: an overview of European approaches, July 2026

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was prompted by the 2026 Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, which led European countries to revise measures for travellers returning from affected areas. The knowledge gap addressed was the lack of standardized European approaches for screening and monitoring these travellers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared current procedures and protocols with those implemented during the 2013-2016 Ebola outbreak. It focused on European approaches for travellers returning from Bundibugyo virus-affected countries.
analysis.methods: The study involved a comparative analysis of national policies and protocols, examining changes and convergences in approaches over time.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that despite some national differences, policies have largely converged towards risk-based management, early case detection, rapid isolation, exposure-based monitoring and healthcare preparedness, rather than routine border screening.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the convergence as a shift towards more targeted and efficient public health measures. The novelty lies in documenting this convergence and highlighting the abandonment of routine border screening in favor of risk-based strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform European public health strategies for managing travellers returning from Bundibugyo virus-affected regions, emphasizing preparedness and targeted monitoring over border screening.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a comparative review of policies without primary data collection or validation of implementation outcomes. The strength of the evidence is moderate, relying on documented protocols rather than empirical results.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines European approaches to screening and monitoring travellers returning from Bundibugyo virus-affected countries following the 2026 Ebola outbreak. It compares current protocols with those from the 2013-2016 Ebola outbreak, finding a convergence towards risk-based management, early detection, isolation, exposure-based monitoring, and healthcare preparedness. Routine border screening has largely been abandoned in favor of these targeted strategies. The authors interpret this shift as an improvement in public health efficiency and preparedness. The findings are significant for informing European public health policies on traveller management during outbreaks, though the evidence is based on policy comparisons rather than empirical data.

title: Exploring the Potential Contribution of Climate-Informed Research to Future Ebola Preparedness in Central Africa

analysis.research_question_and_background: The ongoing 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo highlights the continued vulnerability of Central Africa to recurrent Ebola emergence. This study explores the potential contribution of climate-informed research to future Ebola preparedness in the region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary that reviews current surveillance systems and research on environmental and climatic information related to Ebola emergence in Central Africa.
analysis.methods: The commentary integrates findings from recent modeling studies and emphasizes the need for continued research combining environmental monitoring, remote sensing, ecological observations, and epidemiological data.
analysis.main_results: Recent modeling studies have demonstrated that environmental drivers of Ebola emergence remain highly context-dependent and cannot yet support operational early warning systems.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The commentary argues that climate-informed research could improve understanding of Ebola emergence and contribute to future preparedness strategies, but current evidence is insufficient for operational prediction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the potential of climate-informed research to enhance Ebola preparedness, emphasizing the need for further validation before operational implementation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence remains insufficient to identify validated environmental indicators or operational thresholds capable of predicting Ebola spillover events, indicating a need for further research.

analysis.summary_en: The ongoing 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo underscores the vulnerability of Central Africa to recurrent Ebola emergence. This commentary explores the potential of climate-informed research to enhance future Ebola preparedness. Current surveillance systems are largely reactive, focusing on detecting human cases post-spillover. While strengthening health systems and diagnostic capacity is crucial, environmental and climatic information may contribute to a broader understanding of spillover risk within a One Health framework. However, current evidence is insufficient to identify validated environmental indicators or operational thresholds for predicting Ebola spillover events. Recent modeling studies show that environmental drivers of Ebola emergence are highly context-dependent and cannot yet support operational early warning systems. The commentary argues for continued research integrating environmental monitoring, remote sensing, ecological observations, and epidemiological data to improve understanding of Ebola emergence and contribute to future preparedness strategies. It emphasizes that climate-informed preparedness approaches should be viewed as a complementary research priority requiring further validation before operational implementation.

title: Design of Epitope-Focused Vaccines via Epitope Cleavage

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the challenge of developing broad-spectrum vaccines against pathogens with high genetic variability by focusing on epitope cleavage to steer antibody responses away from specific epitopes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed two independent approaches, circular permutation and proteolytic cleavage, to design vaccine candidates targeting sarbecovirus and Ebolavirus.
analysis.methods: The methods involved designing a sarbecovirus vaccine candidate by circularly permuting the RBD of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and creating broad Ebolavirus immunogens by inserting a TEV protease cleavage site into the glycan cap of Ebola GP.
analysis.main_results: The study found that both the circularly permuted RBD and cleaved GPs elicited antibodies with enhanced cross-reactivity to related viruses and reduced antibody responses toward the cleaved epitope.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating that epitope cleavage can redirect antibody responses without compromising immunogenicity, presenting a novel vaccine design strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a new approach for developing broad-spectrum vaccines that could improve vaccine efficacy against genetically diverse pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not report specific limitations or evidence strength, but the abstract-only evidence limits the assessment of the overall robustness of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: The study introduces epitope cleavage as a strategy to design epitope-focused immunogens that steer antibody responses away from specific epitopes. The researchers demonstrated this approach using two methods: circular permutation of the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and proteolytic cleavage of the glycan cap of Ebola glycoprotein (GP). Both methods resulted in enhanced cross-reactivity to related viruses and reduced antibody responses toward the cleaved epitope. The authors suggest that epitope cleavage can redirect antibody responses without compromising immunogenicity, offering a novel strategy for developing broad-spectrum vaccines against pathogens with high genetic variability. The findings highlight the potential of this approach for improving vaccine efficacy, although the abstract-only evidence limits a comprehensive assessment of the study's robustness.
